title: Calling Parent Methods with super() - Quiz

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of calling `super().__init__()` in a child class constructor?
options: To delete the parent class attributes
To ensure the parent class's constructor runs and initializes inherited attributes
To create a new instance of the parent class
To prevent the child class from accessing parent methods
questions.explanation: When a child class defines its own `__init__`, the parent's `__init__` is not automatically called. `super().__init__()` explicitly calls the parent constructor to initialize inherited attributes.
The correct syntax in Python 3 is `super().__init__(color)`. This calls the parent class's `__init__` method and passes the required arguments.

questions.question: What will happen if a child class defines its own `__init__` method but DOES NOT call `super().__init__()`?
options: The parent class's `__init__` will still run automatically
The program will crash immediately with a syntax error
The parent class's `__init__` will NOT run, and inherited attributes may not be initialized
Python will create a default constructor automatically
questions.explanation: When a child defines its own `__init__`, it overrides the parent's constructor. The parent's `__init__` is not called automatically, so any initialization code in the parent (like setting attributes) will not execute unless explicitly called with `super()`.
